candidates.similarity: Abraham is associated with instruction to descendants in divine ways.
candidates.difference: Genesis reports God's characterization of Abraham and his household; Q 2:132 gives Abraham and Jacob a direct injunction to their sons.
candidates.caveat: Not the same speech; do not present as a verbatim parallel.

candidates.similarity: Jacob gathers and addresses his sons near his death.
candidates.difference: Genesis 49 gives prophetic pronouncements over sons; it does not ask whom they will worship after Jacob's death.
candidates.caveat: A narrative setting overlap, not an identical episode dialogue.

candidates.similarity: The Hebrew narrative names Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob and distinguishes their familial relations.
candidates.difference: Genesis 17 specifies Isaac as covenant successor while blessing Ishmael; Q 2:136 presents a confession encompassing multiple prophetic figures and Q 2:140 contests later religious labels.
candidates.caveat: Genealogical context, not a direct equivalent of Qur'anic confession or a proof of historical dependence.
